extracted.intended_audience: practicing scientists, members of scientific societies, and readers of Nature (general scientific readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for producing and judging scientific work (books, experiments, expeditions, and scientific interpretation), including discussion of scientific method, virtues of investigators, and how scientific conclusions attain credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole question, however, is primarily one of facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions of scientific works must be established by facts; establishment of factual evidence can overturn existing theory and create major revolutions in organic philosophy. Facts can also relieve theoretical difficulties and neutralise objections to prevailing theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage to take up unpopular subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Every lover of science must admire the courage and energy with which Dr. Bastian has taken up an unpopular subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willingness to tackle topics outside mainstream interest is a positive quality in scientific work and warrants respect even before full acceptance of conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skill and patience in experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The skill and patience with which he has experimented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough, careful experimental work is highlighted as a core virtue; experimentation should be conducted with technical competence and perseverance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence in collecting prior observations
rubrics_metrics.description: The labour which he has bestowed in collecting the records of widely scattered and almost forgotten observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive compilation and consideration of previous observations and literature is an important part of producing credible scientific claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical force and philosophical spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: The logical force as well as the philosophical spirit with which he has worked out his conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions should be worked out with both rigorous logical argument and a reflective, philosophically aware approach—showing coherence and attention to broader implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work should provoke renewed observation and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a book that cannot be ignored, and must inevitably lead to renewed discussions and repeated observations, and through these to the establishment of truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuable scientific contributions stimulate further empirical work and debate; provoking follow-up testing and discourse is a sign of productive research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific interpretation must be verifiable and publicly communicable
rubrics_metrics.description: The Philosopher’s interpretation of Nature seems less individual ... because it is based on facts which any one may verify, and is elaborated by reasoning processes of which all admit the validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific claims should be grounded in observations others can check and in reasoning steps acceptable to the community; this communal verifiability distinguishes scientific interpretation from purely individual artistic or poetic readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for truth over adherence to a system
rubrics_metrics.description: The real Philosopher ... always loves Truth better than his System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should abandon appealing theoretical constructs when they conflict with observation; intellectual humility and readiness to revise theories are essential virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of observation, mathematics, and prediction to justify theory
rubrics_metrics.description: In the 'exact' Sciences ... data afforded by precise methods of observation can be made the basis of reasoning ... the final deduction is justified either by its conformity to known or ascertainable facts ... by the fulfilment of the predictions it has sanctioned ... or ... by the actual discovery of phenomena till then unrecognised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification of theories comes from (a) matching known facts, (b) successful predictions being borne out, and (c) discovery of previously unknown phenomena anticipated by the theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware hidden intellectual assumptions in reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: We cannot proceed a step without translating the actual Phenomena of Nature into Intellectual Representations of those phenomena ... the coincidence of its results with the facts of observation is far from proving the Intellectual process to have been correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific reasoning involves conceptual translations and assumptions; agreement with observation does not guarantee that the internal intellectual process or causal story is correct—be cautious about unexamined assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject intellectual arrogance and unjustified claims of fixed laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who set up their own conceptions of the Orderly Sequence ... as fixed and determinate Laws ... are really guilty of the Intellectual arrogance they condemn in the Systems of the Ancients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating provisional or personal conceptual schemes as absolute laws; maintain epistemic modesty about the universality and immutability of proposed laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different modes of interpretation have different standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Artist serves as the Interpreter of Nature ... the Poet ... the Philosopher’s interpretation ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that art, poetry, and science interpret Nature by different aims and criteria: art awakens perception of beauty, poetry evokes moral/emotional impressions, and science seeks verifiable, generalizable accounts—evaluation standards should match the mode of interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific consensus arises from shared method and progressive correction
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an ever-increasing tendency towards agreement among those who use [the scientific method] aright—temporary differences of interpretation being removed ... and lines of pursuit ... found to lead at last to one common goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convergence of views is a product of common methods, improved mastery of observational language, and correction over time; agreement signals reliability but is contingent on method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reasonable assumptions when data are incomplete but treat them as approximations
rubrics_metrics.description: The inadequacy of the basis afforded by actual observation of the perturbations of Uranus required that it should be supplemented by an assumption of the probable distance of the disturbing Planet beyond, which has been shown by subsequent observation to have been only an approximation to the truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When direct data are insufficient, supplement with plausible assumptions to make progress, but recognise and communicate their provisional and approximate character; later observations may revise them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational and institutional responsibility to encourage training
rubrics_metrics.description: The most substantial aid ... would be the setting apart of a number of free benches in the Society’s laboratory for students who ... might desire to continue their studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific societies and institutions should actively support training (e.g., endowed student places, laboratory access) as part of their duty to advance science and cultivate future practitioners.
